howWeWork.title: How a Callaz campaign actually runs
howWeWork.lead: Outbound fails quietly. A campaign can look busy for two months and produce nothing, and by the time that is obvious the budget is gone. The whole method below exists to shorten the distance between a decision and the evidence that it was wrong.
howWeWork.metricsNote: These are the operating targets every campaign is run against and reported on. They describe how we work, not results from past clients.

phases.title: From brief to steady state
phases.lead: Typical timings for a first campaign. A second campaign for the same client usually skips most of phase one.

items.title: Brief and criteria
items.body: We work out what you are selling, to whom, and what a result has to look like before it counts as one. This is the phase people want to skip, and skipping it is why campaigns get argued about later.
outputs: Written definition of a qualified result

items.title: Build
items.body: Script, objection handling, list and system access are prepared. Nothing goes live until you have read the script and agreed it sounds like your company.

items.title: Pilot
items.body: A fixed volume at agreed hours. You listen to real recordings in week one, not curated highlights, and we adjust the script while the campaign is running rather than afterwards.
outputs: Weekly report from the first week
Written read on whether to continue

items.title: Scale and steady state
items.body: The parts that worked get more hours. The parts that did not get rewritten or dropped. Reported weekly, reviewed monthly, and the agreement stays monthly so stopping is always available.
outputs: Monthly review with the team lead
Quarterly recommendation on where to aim next

principles.title: Five things we do not negotiate on
principles.lead: These cost us work occasionally. They are also the reason clients stay past the pilot.

recordedCalls.title: Every call is recorded
recordedCalls.body: All of them, available to you, not a selection we picked. It is the only honest way to judge whether the quality matches the numbers.

namedTeam.title: A named team
namedTeam.body: You know who calls for you. They learn your product properly, and you can speak to them directly rather than through an account manager.

weeklyReporting.title: Weekly reporting
weeklyReporting.body: One page, same format, every week from week one. Dials, conversations, results, and what the market pushed back on.

gdprByDefault.title: GDPR by default
gdprByDefault.body: Processing agreement before the first call, documented lawful basis, working opt-out, and data returned or deleted at the end.

noLockIn.title: No lock-in
noLockIn.body: Monthly terms. If we stop being worth the money, you should be able to act on that immediately, and you can.

compliance.title: The rules we work under
compliance.lead: Outbound calling is regulated, and the regulation differs by market. Getting this wrong is expensive for you, not only for us, so it is agreed in writing before anyone dials.

items.title: Data processing agreement
items.body: Signed before any data changes hands. It sets out what we process, on what basis, for how long, and what happens to it when the campaign ends.

items.title: Lawful basis, documented
items.body: B2B calling under legitimate interest with a written assessment, or consent where the market requires it. Either way it is written down, not assumed.

items.title: Opt-out honoured immediately
items.body: A refusal is recorded on the call and suppressed across every campaign we run for you. In Denmark that includes checking against the Robinson list for consumer campaigns.

items.title: Access control
items.body: Named user accounts in your systems, no shared logins, and access revoked the day a campaign ends or a team member leaves.

items.title: Retention and deletion
items.body: Recordings and campaign data are kept for the period agreed in the processing agreement, then deleted. You can ask for the data back at any point.

faq.q: How quickly can a campaign start?
faq.a: Brief to first call is targeted at 48 hours for a straightforward campaign where you already have a list and a clear offer. A campaign that needs list building and a new script is realistically one to two weeks.

Pricing depends on hours, languages and how much setup the campaign needs, so a number quoted before we have heard the offer would be meaningless. You get a written proposal with the scope priced out before anything is signed.

faq.q: Can we listen to calls live?
faq.a: Yes. Live listening can be arranged for your own team, and it is worth doing in the first week. Most clients hear something in the first hour that changes their script.

faq.q: What happens to our data when we stop?
faq.a: It is returned in your format and then deleted from our systems within the period set in the processing agreement. You get written confirmation when the deletion is done.

faq.q: Do you work with our existing agency or in-house team?
faq.a: Frequently. Overflow alongside an in-house team is one of the most common setups, and it avoids the disruption of moving everything at once.

industries.title: Sectors we take campaigns in
industries.lead: Experience in a sector matters less than most agencies claim, and more than nothing. What actually transfers is knowing the objections before you hear them, and knowing which rules apply before you dial.

energy.title: Energy and utilities
energy.body: Switching campaigns and contract renewal, where consent handling and clear price presentation decide whether a sale survives the cooling-off period.

telecom.title: Telecom
telecom.body: Business subscriptions and upgrades. High volume, short calls, and a market that has heard every opener before.

saas.title: Software and SaaS
saas.body: Appointment setting into demo calls. The job is filtering hard so the demo team spends its hours on accounts that can actually buy.

insurance.title: Insurance and finance
insurance.body: Advisory meetings rather than closing on the call, since the regulated part belongs with your own licensed people.

trades.title: Trades and installation
trades.body: Local B2B and follow-up on quotes that went quiet. A short call recovers a surprising share of them.

logistics.title: Transport and logistics
logistics.body: Freight and warehousing where the decision maker is rarely at a desk and the calling window is narrow.

membership.title: Membership organisations
membership.body: Recruitment and renewal for unions and trade associations, where tone matters more than pace.

nonprofit.title: Non-profit
nonprofit.body: Supporter contact and renewal, run under the stricter consent rules that apply to fundraising.

adapt.title: Three things we adjust every time
adapt.lead: The method stays the same. These three move, and getting them wrong is what makes a campaign in a new sector underperform.

items.title: The calling window
items.body: A site manager and a finance director are reachable at opposite ends of the day. Calling at the wrong hour looks like a bad list.

items.title: The rules that apply
items.body: Consumer campaigns, financial services and fundraising each carry requirements that B2B software does not. We check before the first dial, not after a complaint.

items.title: What counts as qualified
items.body: A qualified meeting for a SaaS demo and a qualified meeting for a freight contract have almost nothing in common. The definition gets rewritten for every campaign.

honesty.title: If your sector is not here, it is not a problem
honesty.body: This list is where we have run campaigns, not a limit on where we can. What actually decides whether outbound works is the offer, the list and the margin, and those you can assess in a twenty-minute call regardless of the industry label on your company.

about.title: A contact centre built the way we wanted to be treated as clients
about.lead: Callaz was founded in Kolding in 2025 by people who had spent enough time inside phone floors to know exactly which parts of the industry deserve their reputation.

story.title: Why this company exists
paragraphs: Most companies that buy outbound have bought it before and been disappointed. The pattern repeats: an impressive pitch, a team you never meet, a monthly report that is mostly activity counts, and a slow realisation that nobody can tell you whether it is working.

Callaz is built to make that specific failure hard. Every call is recorded and available to you. The team calling for you has names you know. The report arrives weekly from week one and says what did not work as plainly as what did. And the agreement is monthly, so if we stop earning it you can act immediately rather than waiting out a contract.
We are a young company and we do not pretend otherwise. What we can promise is the part that is entirely within our control: how we work, what you can see, and what happens when something goes wrong.

values.title: Three commitments that shape the rest
values.lead: These are not aspirations on a wall. Each one has a mechanism behind it that you can check.

items.title: Say no to the wrong work
items.body: If we do not think outbound will work for your offer, we say so on the first call. Taking a campaign that will fail costs us a reference and costs you a quarter.

items.title: Show the bad numbers first
items.body: The weekly report leads with what is not working. A report that only contains good news is not a report, it is marketing.

items.title: Treat the brand as borrowed
items.body: We call in your name, which means every conversation spends a little of your reputation. That is why calls are recorded, sampled and scored rather than just counted.

offices.title: Registered in Kolding, calling across Denmark
offices.lead: The registered office is in Kolding, and that is where the campaigns are run from. We call nationwide.

contact.title: Talk to a person who can actually answer
contact.lead: No gatekeeping and no discovery form before you get a human. Call, write, or use the form and you will hear back within one working day.

channels.phoneNote: Fastest route. If we cannot take it, we call back the same day.

contact.hoursBody: Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:00 Central European Time. Campaign hours are set per client and can extend beyond this.
contact.formLead: The more specific you are about the market and the offer, the more useful the first reply will be.

quote.title: A written proposal, not a sales sequence
quote.lead: Tell us what you sell, where, and roughly how much volume you are after. You get a proposal with scope, team size, pricing and a start date, and if outbound is the wrong tool for your offer we will tell you that instead.

steps.title: You send this form
steps.body: Market, offer and volume. Two sentences is enough to start.

steps.title: Twenty-minute call
steps.body: We ask the questions that actually change the price, and give you an honest read on fit.

steps.title: Written proposal
steps.body: Scope, pricing, start date and what a qualified result is defined as. Within two working days of the call.

assurances: No obligation and no follow-up sequence
We will say if outbound is wrong for your offer
Your details are used to reply and nothing else

faq.q: What do you need from me to quote?
faq.a: The market, what you sell, who buys it, and roughly what volume you have in mind. If you have an existing list or CRM, mention it, because it usually changes both the price and the approach.

Mostly a monthly rate based on hours and languages, sometimes with a performance element on top. Pilots are priced as a fixed project. We do not do commission-only, because it produces the wrong behaviour on the phone.
Monthly after the pilot. There is no annual lock-in, and there is no clause that makes leaving awkward.
Brief to first call is targeted at 48 hours when the list and the offer are ready. Add a week or two if the list needs building.

faq.q: Will I be added to a mailing list?
faq.a: No. Your details are used to answer this enquiry. There is no newsletter and nothing is passed to anyone else.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lead: This policy explains what personal data Callaz collects through this website, why, and what rights you have. It is written to be read rather than to be technically unassailable.

sections.title: What we collect
paragraphs: If you send an enquiry through a form on this site, we collect the name, company, email address, optional phone number, the topic you selected and the message you wrote.

Our server also processes technical data that every web request carries, including your IP address and browser type. This is used to serve the page and to limit automated abuse of the enquiry form. It is not used to build a profile of you.
This site loads no third-party scripts, no advertising tags and no social media widgets. Nothing about your visit is shared with another company as a result of you reading this page.

sections.title: Why we use it
paragraphs: Enquiry data is used for one purpose: to answer your enquiry and, if it leads somewhere, to prepare a proposal. The lawful basis is our legitimate interest in responding to someone who contacted us, and, where a business relationship follows, the performance of a contract.
We do not use enquiry data for marketing. You will not be added to a mailing list because you asked a question, and your details are never sold or passed to a third party for their own purposes.

sections.title: Cookies
paragraphs: We set one strictly necessary cookie that records your cookie choice, so you are not asked again on every page. It contains only the choice itself and expires after twelve months.

Statistics cookies are only set if you accept them in the banner. You can change or withdraw your choice at any time using the cookie settings link in the footer, and withdrawing consent is as easy as giving it.

Your choice of light or dark appearance is kept in browser localStorage under the key callaz-theme. It is a strictly necessary setting you selected yourself, it never leaves your browser, and clearing your browsing data removes it.

sections.title: How long we keep it
paragraphs: Enquiries that do not lead to a business relationship are deleted after twelve months. Enquiries that do become part of the client record and are kept for as long as the relationship lasts, plus the period required by Danish bookkeeping law.
Server logs are kept for a short technical retention period and then discarded.

sections.title: Who else sees it
paragraphs: We use a small number of processors to run the site and deliver email, and they only process data on our instructions under a data processing agreement. We do not sell data, and we do not share it with advertisers.
Where a processor is located outside the EU or EEA, the transfer is covered by the European Commission standard contractual clauses.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: Under the GDPR you have the right to access the personal data we hold about you, to have it corrected, to have it deleted, to have processing restricted, to object to processing based on legitimate interest, and to receive your data in a portable format.
Write to the address in the panel on this page and we will answer within one month. There is no charge for exercising these rights.
If you are not satisfied with how we handle your data you can complain to the Danish Data Protection Agency, Datatilsynet, Carl Jacobsens Vej 35, 2500 Valby, datatilsynet.dk.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: If this policy changes materially we will update the date at the top and, where the change affects how we use data you have already given us, we will contact you directly rather than rely on you rereading this page.
